arxiv-2108-03279.title: Radiative corrections to semileptonic beta decays: Progress and challenges
arxiv-2108-03279.creator: Chien-Yeah Seng 1
arxiv-2108-03279.description: Abstract We review some recent progress in the theory of electroweak radiative corrections in semileptonic decay processes. The resurrection of the so-called Sirlin’s representation based on current algebra relations permits a clear separation between the perturbatively-calculable and incalculable pieces in the 𝒪 ⁡ ( G F ​ α ) \mathcal{O}(G_{F}\alpha) radiative corrections.

arxiv-2110-14126.description: Abstract Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides an information-theoretically secure method to share keys between legitimate users. To achieve large-scale deployment of QKD, it should be easily scalable and cost-effective. The infrastructure construction of quantum access network (QAN) expands network capacity and the integration between QKD and classical optical communications reduces the cost of channel.

arxiv-2204-12915.title: Improving Feature Generalizability with Multitask Learning in Class Incremental Learning
arxiv-2204-12915.creator: Dong Ma, Chi Ian Tang, Cecilia Mascolo
arxiv-2204-12915.description: Abstract Many deep learning applications, like keyword spotting [ 1 , 2 ] , require the incorporation of new concepts (classes) over time, referred to as Class Incremental Learning (CIL). The major challenge in CIL is catastrophic forgetting, i.e., preserving as much of the old knowledge as possible while learning new tasks.

arxiv-2206-12632.title: A 6-chromatic odd-distance graph in the plane
arxiv-2206-12632.creator: Jaan Parts
arxiv-2206-12632.description: Abstract Two vertices of an odd-distance graph are connected by an edge if and only if their Euclidean distance is an odd integer. We construct a 6-chromatic odd-distance graph in the plane. 1 Introduction Motivation. This work was motivated by Marijn Heule (and partly by Dire Straits with their song ”Money for Nothing ”).

arxiv-2303-02112.title: Stealthy Perception-based Attacks on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles*
arxiv-2303-02112.creator: Amir Khazraei, Haocheng Meng, Miroslav Pajic
arxiv-2303-02112.description: Abstract In this work, we study vulnerability of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to stealthy attacks on perception-based control. To guide our analysis, we consider two specific missions: ( i i ) ground vehicle tracking (GVT), and ( i ​ i ii ) vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) of a quadcopter on a moving ground vehicle.

arxiv-2308-14888.title: The error term in counting prime pairs
arxiv-2308-14888.creator: Leon Chou, Summer Haag, Jake Huryn, Andrew Ledoan
arxiv-2308-14888.description: Abstract . We relate the size of the error term in the Hardy–Littlewood conjectured formula for the number of prime pairs to the L 1 L^{1} norm of an exponential sum over the primes formed with the von Mangoldt function. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 11N05; Secondary 11P32, 11N36 1.

arxiv-2310-01463.title: Stringy phenomenology with preon models
arxiv-2310-01463.creator: Risto Raitio
arxiv-2310-01463.description: Abstract We compare, following Pati, global symmetries our topological supersymmetric preon model with the heterotic E 8 × E 8 E_{8}\times E_{8} string theory. We include Pati’s supergravity based preon model in this work and compare the preon interactions of his model to ours.

arxiv-2412-00692.title: MCBLT: Multi-Camera Multi-Object 3D Tracking in Long Videos
arxiv-2412-00692.creator: Yizhou Wang, Tim Meinhardt, Orcun Cetintas, Cheng-Yen Yang, Sameer S. Pusegaonkar, Benjamin Missaoui, Sujit Biswas, Zheng Tang, Laura Leal-Taixé
arxiv-2412-00692.description: Abstract Object perception from multi-view cameras is crucial for intelligent systems, particularly in indoor environments, e.g . , warehouses, retail stores, and hospitals. Most traditional multi-target multi-camera (MTMC) detection and tracking methods rely on 2D object detection, single-view multi-object tracking (MOT), and cross-view re-identification (ReID) techniques, without properly handling important 3D information by multi-view image aggregation.

arxiv-2505-00477.title: Orbit-blocking words in free groups
arxiv-2505-00477.creator: Lucy Koch-Hyde, Siobhan O’Connor, Éamonn Olive, Vladimir Shpilrain
arxiv-2505-00477.description: Abstract . By strengthening known results about primitivity-blocking words in free groups, we prove that for any nontrivial element w w of a free group of finite rank, there are words that cannot be subwords of any cyclically reduced automorphic image of w w . This has implications for the average-case complexity of Whitehead’s problem. 1.

arxiv-2505-18362.title: Maximum Principle of Optimal Probability Density Control
arxiv-2505-18362.creator: Nathan Gaby, Xiaojing Ye
arxiv-2505-18362.description: Abstract We develop a general theoretical framework for optimal probability density control on standard measure spaces, aimed at addressing large-scale multi-agent control problems. In particular, we establish a maximum principle (MP) for control problems posed on infinite-dimensional spaces of probability distributions and control vector fields.

arxiv-2506-09947.title: KI4Demokratie : An AI-Based Platform for Monitoring and Fostering Democratic Discourse
arxiv-2506-09947.creator: Rudy Alexandro Garrido Veliz, Till Nikolaus Schaland, Simon Bergmoser, Florian Horwege, Somya Bansal, Ritesh Nahar, Martin Semmann, Jörg Forthmann, Seid Muhie Yimam
arxiv-2506-09947.description: Abstract Social media increasingly fuel extremism, especially right-wing extremism, and enable the rapid spread of antidemocratic narratives. Although AI and data science are often leveraged to manipulate political opinion, there is a critical need for tools that support effective monitoring without infringing on freedom of expression.

arxiv-2602-03753.title: Test-Time Conditioning with Representation-Aligned Visual Features
arxiv-2602-03753.creator: Nicolas Sereyjol-Garros, Ellington Kirby, Victor Letzelter, Victor Besnier, Nermin Samet
arxiv-2602-03753.description: Abstract While representation alignment with self-supervised models has been shown to improve diffusion model training, its potential for enhancing inference-time conditioning remains largely unexplored. We introduce Representation-Aligned Guidance (REPA-G), a framework that leverages these aligned representations, with rich semantic properties, to enable test-time conditioning from features in generation.
